prompt: Here's a service that runs a leader-only background job (a cron/reconciler) across several identical replicas, using Redis for leader election with a TTL-based lease — a follower wins the lock with `SET key myId NX PX ttl`, and the current leader is supposed to keep renewing that lease on a periodic tick. Everything passes on the happy path, but after any lease-expiry event (a network blip, a GC pause, a partition) operators see two replicas that both report `isLeader = true` and both run the leader-only job at the same time — a split brain. Read through `LeaderElector` below and tell me exactly why the renew path lets a demoted node keep extending a lease it no longer owns, then describe the fix and a test that would catch this.
